let S4 := Equiv.Perm (Fin 4)

let K := H ⊓ MulAction.stabilizer S4 (2 : Fin 4)
let left : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding H G :=
  MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator 1 (fun _ => Subgroup.mem_top _)
let right : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding K H :=
  MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator 1 (by
    intro k
    simpa only [one_mul, inv_one, mul_one] using
      (inf_le_left : K ≤ H) (Subtype.property k))
let leftWire := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary
  (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up left))
let merge := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent (R := Complex)
  (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.mergeUp left right)
let rightDot := MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.upDrawing
  (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.identity (R := Complex) right)
let trunkDot := MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.upDrawing
  (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.identity (R := Complex)
    (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp left right))
let rightMarked := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
  (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal leftWire rightDot) merge
let trunkMarked := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical merge trunkDot
let A₄ : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.Shapes (U := S4) Complex boundary :=

    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up embedding))

Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, §3.3, Proposition 3.2 [prop:preorder-not-symmetric], p. 10. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. Forward replacement holds for every ambient group. Example 3.2 places the standard inclusions in the finitary symmetric group and takes S₄ as the outer boundary group G. For the reverse failure, Lean uses the finite realization with Equiv.Perm (Fin 4) as ambient group and its top subgroup as G, with the same boundary inclusions and composite. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf#page=10

The owner clarification of 27 November 2026, recorded in translation recheck request f13b4bd8ba9fe139, gives every marked vertex a finite complex linear combination of termwise eligible group elements. A group-element dot is the coefficient-one singleton. The identity-labelled drawings witness the two shapes at the ordered boundary of two upward inputs and one upward output. ShapeReplaces ranges over the full PlanarAtBoundary fibers at fixed boundary groups and strand cosets and compares the evaluations of the stored diagrams. InductionMergeDotSlide supplies the forward slide term by term. RightInputDotSlideObstruction records that every supported term of a right-input label maps into the embedded H and that the coefficient-one trunk label is supported at (3 4), which lies outside H.

The designated article defect report returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. No correction to the statement of Proposition 3.2 was available. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects
